task: Make the Zoo playthrough harness deterministic and frame-aware so the same code gives the same verdict every run
requirements: Add read-only fields to the Zoo debug snapshot (debugSnapshot in src/minigames/zoo/index.js): `elapsed` (sum of clamped game dt in seconds) and `frame` (count of update() calls while active). No gameplay change.

Rewrite the route walker (walkSegment in scripts/playthrough-zoo.mjs): keep movement keys held until the player's position has progressed or a game-time budget has elapsed, and judge a stall by game `elapsed`/`frame` advancing without progress, not by wall-clock pulse length or number of ui() samples. A key must never be released before at least one game update has applied it.

Any step that presses Space/interact after walking (showPhoto, photographing at a viewpoint) must first verify the player actually arrived; if not, record that step and every dependent check as HARNESS_PRECONDITION_FAILED instead of pressing from far away.

Fixed check registry: each section registers its expected check names up front; checks skipped because a precondition failed are reported as HARNESS_PRECONDITION_FAILED. For the same selected sections the total check count is identical on every run (no `if (s) check(...)` or `continue` that makes checks vanish).

Seed Math.random in the page through the browser init script with a logged seed (default fixed, overridable with env ZOO_SEED), so the same seed gives the same visitor spots, models and wanted animals.
Close each section's browser context/page when that section finishes.
Keep every existing assertion's intent; do not remove or weaken checks.

Claude already changed showPhotoToVisitor so a wrong photo is used up on refusal (SPEC: one photo is one delivery attempt). Update any harness step that assumed a refused photo is still carried, and add a check that a refused photo is no longer carried.
constraints: Do not change Zoo gameplay, movement, collision, layout or visuals; only the two debug fields may be added to src/minigames/zoo/index.js.
Do not touch the Restaurant, Drink Stand, Coloring or Sports harnesses.
Follow ~/.claude/workers/harness/PROTOCOL.md: wait for state, not time; classify preconditions; seeded or invariant-based randomness.
Edit source with structured file edits, never whole-file shell or regex rewrites.
Your sandbox may not be able to start the preview server; do not fake playthrough results. Claude runs the playthrough.
notes: Diagnosis (.ai/codex-diagnosis.md) was checked by Claude: walker pulses of 70-210 ms (playthrough-zoo.mjs:253) and a 9-sample stall rule (:245) against a game that clamps dt to 0.05 s (zoo/index.js:881) under SwiftShader; conditional checks at the anti-shortcut turnaround and the habitat `continue` explain the varying total (96/108/109). The graph-clearance idea (layout.test.mjs) was judged low confidence and is out of scope. Purpose: the Zoo playthrough must become a trustworthy regression check. The harness is untrusted after this change until Claude sees it pass on known-good and fail on a known-bad condition, so make it easy to force a known-bad (e.g. an env flag that deliberately stops the walker short) without touching product source. Report per section: pass count, total, and the seed used. Record no DESIGN_DECISIONS entry unless you make a product-facing decision.
